notes: The FY25 10-K was reachable (filed 2026-03-11, accession 0002070849-26-000017, main doc blln-20251231.htm, about 495K characters). I read characters 0 to 430K, covering the business section and risk factors. It never names Illumina as a supplier. It has no sequencer counts, no NovaSeq 6000 or X language, no per-test sequencing cost, and no Illumina agreement or purchase-commitment terms. The only Illumina mention is as a NIPT competitor (via Verinata). Supplier language is generic: 'sole- or single-source suppliers' for sequencers, three months of inventory, and one to nine months to replace a supplier. I did not read the last ~65K characters (offset 430000), which likely hold the financial statement notes and a commitments note. I also did not find the MD&A cost-of-revenue discussion in the sections I read, so it may sit in that unread tail. The exhibit list shows no Illumina supply agreement (EX-10.9 and EX-10.15 are unidentified). The one usable datapoint is a gross margin of 68% in FY25 vs 53% in FY24. The filing attributes this to operational efficiency and automation and does not tie it to the X. That is mildly suggestive of falling cost per test, but it is unattributed and weak.
how_to_mine: Fetch https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2070849/000207084926000017/blln-20251231.htm with offset 430000 and read the notes on commitments and concentrations. Also fetch the XBRL R-pages (viewer link in the filing index) for purchase obligations, cost of revenue and test volumes. Check the MD&A cost-of-revenue paragraph. Open EX-10.9 (a109-amendmentno2todevelop.htm) and EX-10.15 to identify the counterparties. Also look at BillionToOne's S-1 (IPO late 2025) for Illumina or sequencer wording, and for the sequencing-cost-per-test and NIPT volume metrics.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: BillionToOne's gross margin jumped to 68% in FY25 from 53% in FY24, which implies much lower cost per test, but the filing credits operations and does not mention the X.
items.detail: The FY25 10-K risk factors state gross margins of 68% and 53% for 2025 and 2024, and say efficiency gains contributed to revenue growth. It does not cite NovaSeq X or sequencing cost as a driver. If the margin gain includes sequencing savings, that is consistent with customers capturing cost deflation instead of reinvesting it in depth. The attribution is unverified, so it is a weak datapoint.
items.quote: gross margin of 68% and 53% for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024
items.why_new: The known list has BillionToOne's cost per test as 'relatively stable' (from a call), not these 10-K margin figures.

new_candidates.source: BillionToOne FY25 10-K tail (offset 430000), XBRL R-pages and EX-10.9/EX-10.15
new_candidates.why: Commitments, concentration and MD&A cost-of-revenue drivers were not reached in the first 430K characters.
